# WGOM Atlantic Cod and GOM Haddock Catch at Length 

**Description**: 

This data contains the proportions of fish caught at length in inches by season for
Western Gulf of Maine (WGOM) Atlantic Cod and Gulf of Maine (GOM) Haddock.
The 'summer' season is May - August and the 'winter' is September - April. 
We provide the medians of 101 random draws of the observed proportions caught at length 
and the fitted (i.e., smoothed) proportions for the baseline year. 

We also provide the median fitted projected catch at length probability distribution 
across 101 draws for the upcoming management cycle. The projected catch at length 
distribution is based on the baseline observed catch at length distribution and the projected 
numbers at age from the stock assessment. 

**Years available**: 

The data are for the baseline regulatory year, also called the calibration year, 
as well as the projection year. Baseline catch at length is based on the most recent 6 waves of data. 
For the 2026 management cycle, baseline catch at length was simulated using data for 
waves 1-5 of 2025 and wave 6 of 2024 and we provide projected catch at length for 2026. 
For the 2027 management cycle, catch at length will be simulated using data 
for waves 1-5 of 2026 and wave 6 of 2025.

## Methods

### Data sources

We get data on catch, effort, and numbers of fish caught at length from the Marine 
Recreational Information Program ([MRIP](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/insight/marine-recreational-information-program)). 
MRIP provides length data for a sample of harvested fish and for a sample of discarded 
fish, the latter of which comes from headboat observations. 

The numbers at age data are from the most recent stock assessment.

### Data extraction 

The data is limited to trips where the angler caught or primarily targeted cod or haddock 
in the WGOM, which includes any Maine or Massachusetts trips taken in statistical areas 
513, 514, 515, 521, and 526, as well as any trips taken from New Hampshire. 
GOM Haddock are assessed in statistical areas 513, 514, 515, 511, and 512, but no Haddock 
are caught in areas 511 and 512 while very few Haddock are caught in areas 521 and 526. 

![Northeast Atlantic Cod Statistical Areas with Stock Areas](stat_areas.jpg)

### Data analysis/Processing

[Data processing code](https://github.com/kimberly-bastille/groundfishRDM/blob/main/Code/pre_sim) 
is in the groundfishRDM repository. 

#### Baseline Catch at Length Distribution

We use the samples of the number of fish discarded at length and harvested at length 
to get baseline probability distributions for both by season for each species. Next, we multiply 
the harvest at length probability distribution by 101 draws of baseline simulated total harvest 
and we multiply the discards at length probability distribution by 101 draws of simulated 
total discards. The simulated baseline total numbers of fish harvested and discarded are based on 
random draws of simulated directed trips and simulated harvest- and discards per trip. 

We add the simulated total harvest and discards at length to get 101 draws of total 
baseline numbers of fish caught at length, and then convert the numbers to proportions which form the 
'observed' catch at length distribution draws. We then fit these observed probabilities 
to a gamma distribution to get smoothed distributions. These fitted probabilities are fed into 
the model. Finally, for the dashboard we take the medians of the 101 draws of baseline observed 
and fitted catch at length probabilities by season for cod and haddock.  

The metric column in the raw data has the season and the length of the fish in inches. 
We receive the fish lengths in centimeters and convert them to inches, which is why
the lengths are non-integers in the raw data. 

#### Projected Catch at Length Distribution

To get the projected catch at length distribution, we compute an empirical selectivity 
at length by species, season, draw, and length based on the baseline observed catch at length 
probabilities and baseline numbers at length. Baseline numbers at length are converted 
from the baseline numbers at age from the stock assessment using age-length keys from 
recent NEFSC trawl survey data.

Next, we convert the projected numbers at age from the stock assessment into projected 
numbers at length using the same age-length keys. We apply the baseline selectivity at length 
to the projected numbers at length to get the projected catch at length in numbers. 
We convert the projected catch at length numbers to probabilities and then fit the 
probabilities to a gamma distribution to get the projected fitted probabilities (i.e., a smoothed distribution). 

Finally, we take the median fitted projected catch at length probabilities   
across 101 draws by season and species to display in the recDST data dashboard. 
The lengths are in inches.
